learning_objective: 🎯 Fuel your body right! Learn what makes a balanced diet, the roles of different nutrients, and how to spot unsafe, adulterated food.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A diet that contains all essential nutrients (carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, water, and roughage) in the correct proportion required by the body.

Macronutrients (Carbs, Proteins, Fats) are needed in large amounts to provide energy and build the body. Micronutrients (Vitamins, Minerals) are needed in small amounts to regulate body functions and immunity.
Water makes up about 60% of our body. It regulates temperature, transports nutrients, flushes out toxins, and is crucial for athletes to prevent dehydration.
The dangerous practice of adding cheaper, harmful substances to food (like chalk in milk or brick powder in chili powder) to increase quantity and profit, which severely harms human health.
Athletes have different dietary needs. They require 'carb-loading' before endurance events for sustained energy and high protein after workouts for muscle recovery.

fun_activity.title: 🧮 Calculate Your BMI
fun_activity.instructions: Measure your weight in Kilograms and height in Meters. Use the formula: BMI = Weight / (Height x Height). A healthy BMI is generally between 18.5 and 24.9!

exam_tips: 📌 Clear up the difference between Macro (Energy-yielding) and Micro (Protective) nutrients.
📌 Know the formula for BMI and what its categories mean (Underweight, Normal, Overweight, Obese).
📌 Give common examples of food adulteration and its health hazards.
quick_recap: ⭐ Carbohydrates are the body's preferred and fastest source of energy.
⭐ Vitamins are classified into fat-soluble (A, D, E, K) and water-soluble (B, C).
⭐ Eating a diverse, colorful plate of food naturally ensures a good intake of micronutrients.
